SPECIFICATION FIRST. The submitted package declares the ladder in three agreeing places: /Users/jt/math-sdk/games/future_spinner/game_config.py:106 `self.bet_levels = [0.10 ... 100.00]`, /Users/jt/math-sdk/games/future_spinner/library/publish_files/game_metadata.json:20-23 `betLevels` [0.10 ... 100.00] with `minBet` 0.10, `maxBet` 100.00, `stepBet` 0.10, and /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/lib/stores/gameStore.ts:7 `BET_LEVELS`. So the closed-form authorised range is 0.10 to 100.00 in 0.10 steps, and the built-in fallback array is not arbitrary, it IS the submitted declaration.

THE MECHANISM, in two halves that only bite together.
(1) THE DROP. rgsService.ts:565-567 converts `config.minBet`, `config.maxBet`, `config.stepBet` into AuthResponse and :569 does the same for `defaultBetLevel`. `initRGS`, the only production caller of `authenticate`, then publishes exactly four things at rgsService.ts:733-737: balance, currency, `rgsBetLevels.set(auth.betLevels)` (:735) and jurisdiction flags. The four limit fields are computed and fall out of scope when the function returns. Nothing non-locked can ever see them.
(2) THE UNCONDITIONAL FALLBACK. /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/lib/stores/betLadder.ts:39-41 is `derived(rgsBetLevels, ($levels) => $levels.length > 0 ? $levels : BET_LEVELS)`. The predicate is EMPTINESS, not session mode. rgsService.ts:568 writes `(config.betLevels ?? []).map(...)`, so an authenticate response that omits `config.betLevels` while still sending `minBet`/`maxBet`/`stepBet` yields an empty array, and a LIVE session then bets off the hardcoded USD-shaped ladder against a wallet whose authorised range we parsed and threw away. /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/lib/stores/rgsBetLevels.ts:14 states the intended reading of empty as "mock/dev mode or auth failure"; that reading is wrong, because a live success with no betLevels is indistinguishable from it.

So the defect is not "the limits are dropped", it is "the limits are dropped AND the only surviving signal, ladder emptiness, cannot distinguish no-RGS from RGS-sent-no-ladder". Either half alone is harmless.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT LOSS ON THE SAME LINE. `defaultBetLevel` (rgsService.ts:569) is also dropped, so the game always opens at gameStore.ts:16's hardcoded 1.00 whatever the platform authorised as the default. That one is partly compensated: HudOverlay.svelte:142-143 snaps an off-ladder bet via `snapBetToLadder()`, so 1.00 is moved onto the RGS ladder rather than wagered off it, but it lands on the NEAREST level (betLadder.ts:44-49), not on the platform's chosen default.

THE MECHANISM. The `lang` URL parameter is parsed TWICE, by two modules, with two different rules, and the two results are sent to two different destinations.

WIRE SIDE, locked. /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/lib/services/rgsService.ts:525 `const lang = p.get('lang') ?? 'en'`. Raw, no case folding, no trim, no validation against the shipped locale set, no social check. It is stored on SessionParams at :529 and `authenticate` puts it on the wire as `language: params.lang` (the request body built in authenticate, asserted in shape by rgsService.contract.test.ts:92).

SCREEN SIDE, non-locked. /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/App.svelte:190-191 re-reads the SAME parameter from the SAME URL and passes it through `resolveLaunchLocale`, which at /Users/jt/math-sdk/frontend/src/lib/stores/socialLocale.ts:73 returns 'en' outright if the session is social, at :76-79 lowercases and trims and requires membership of the shipped locale map, and at :82 falls back to 'en' for anything absent, unknown or malformed.

THE THREE DIVERGENCE CLASSES, derived from those two rule sets, not measured.
  ?lang=da&social=true  -> wire 'da', screen 'en'. socialLocale.test.ts:46 pins the screen half; nothing pins the wire half.
  ?lang=sv              -> wire 'sv', screen 'en' (Swedish is not one of the sixteen shipped).
  ?lang=DE              -> wire 'DE', screen 'de'.
  no lang               -> 'en' both. Agree. This is the ONLY case any existing test exercises.

WHY THE TEST SUITE CANNOT SEE IT. rgsService.contract.test.ts:56 constructs SessionParams by hand with `lang: 'en'` and calls `authenticate` directly, so `parseSessionParams` never runs and the derivation at :525 is never exercised. locale_launch_conformance.mjs:137-138 drives `social=true&lang=da` and `social=true&lang=de` in a real browser but asserts only what RENDERS. So both halves are gated and the join between them is not.

HOW FAR I CAN TAKE THE CONSEQUENCE, and no further. The only language requirement in the mirror is /Users/jt/math-sdk/docs/stake-engine-live/rgs-communication.md:26, quoted: "English is the only required language. If only English (en) is supported, on-screen text must not corrupt when other language parameters are passed." That is a requirement on RENDERING and resolveLaunchLocale satisfies it. The mirror says nothing about what the RGS does with the `language` field of the authenticate request, so the SIZE of the harm (platform-side localised wallet errors, session records, operator reporting) is UNKNOWN. What is DERIVED and certain is that the game declares one language to the platform while rendering another, including in social mode where guideline item 46 requires English.

ONE MORE THING ON THE SAME LINES, minor. `device` is parsed at rgsService.ts:521-523 and stored at :530, and is then read by nothing: it is on no request body and no consumer exists outside replayService.ts:115, which does its own independent parse. Dead field in the locked file.
